values.label: Survey, geotech and planning
values.source_title: Data Center Construction: Costs, Timeline, and Delivery Steps
values.quote: Planning & Feasibility: 3-6 months
values.note: Planning and feasibility phase, which carries the survey and geotechnical work. Industry guide (secondary).

values.label: Design and engineering to permit and order release
values.source_title: Data Center Construction: Costs, Timeline, and Delivery Steps
values.quote: Design: 6-12 months
values.note: Low end of the 6 to 12 month design phase (industry guide, secondary): early design packages release the building permit and the long-lead orders; design continues alongside construction.

values.label: Zoning and approvals
values.source_title: Data Center Construction: Costs, Timeline, and Delivery Steps
values.quote: Permits & Approvals: 6-18 months
values.note: Permits and approvals phase. Industry guide (secondary).

values.label: Zoning and site plan, Virginia
values.source_title: Commercial Development Committee Presentation, July 15, 2026
values.quote: 129 county days, and 269 applicant/outside-agency days
values.note: Prince William County FY26 elapsed site-plan time; Loudoun ended by-right data centers in March 2025, so a rezoning case is the norm

values.label: Building permit
values.source_title: Commercial Development Committee Presentation, July 15, 2026
values.quote: 152 county days and 128 applicant/outside-agency days, with 3.71 reviews
values.note: 152 county review days for major new construction in Prince William County, in months, used as the US default.

values.label: Air permit, minor source
values.source_title: Data Center Webinar: Virginia Air Permitting
values.quote: Synthetic Minor NSR: 4-6 months
values.note: synthetic minor permit, Virginia DEQ timeline as reported by a permitting consultancy, used as the US default; standby generators alone usually stay minor.

values.label: Air permit, major source (PSD and Title V)
values.source_title: Data Center Webinar: Virginia Air Permitting
values.quote: Major NSR (PSD) + Title V: 1-2 years
values.note: PSD plus Title V, Virginia timeline, used as the US default; onsite gas turbines or engine fleets at data-center scale are usually major sources.

values.label: Air permit, minor source, Texas
values.source_title: Fact Sheet - Air Quality Permitting (Target Time Frames)
values.quote: Standard Permits with public notice: 150 days
values.note: TCEQ standard permit with notice, 150 target days / 30.44.

values.label: Air permit, major source, Texas
values.source_title: Fact Sheet - Air Quality Permitting (Target Time Frames)
values.quote: Federal New Source Review (PSD, Nonattainment, 112g): 330 days
values.note: TCEQ federal NSR (PSD) target 330 days / 30.44.

values.label: Air permit, major source, Arizona
values.source_title: Rule 210 - Title V Permit Provisions
values.quote: within 18 months after receiving a complete application
values.note: Maricopa County Title V final action.

values.label: Air permit, minor source, Arizona
values.source_title: Rule 220 - Non-Title V Permit Provisions
values.quote: in no case longer than nine months after receiving a complete application
values.note: Maricopa non-Title V final action 90 to 270 days; midpoint / 30.44.

values.label: Air permit, minor source, Pennsylvania
values.source_title: Data Center Webinar: Pennsylvania Air Permitting
values.quote: Minor source: approx. 6-9 months

values.label: Air permit, major source, Pennsylvania
values.source_title: Data Center Webinar: Pennsylvania Air Permitting
values.quote: Major source: approx. 9-15 months

values.label: Cooling-water discharge permit (NPDES)
values.source_title: Individual Permit - NPDES (Permit Handbook)
values.publisher: Washington Governor's Office for Regulatory Innovation and Assistance
values.quote: Average days from Receipt to Complete: 210
values.note: Washington individual NPDES, 210 days receipt-to-complete plus 36 days public notice, in months, used as the US default for tower cooling

values.label: Large-load interconnection study
values.source_title: FERC Rulemakings on Large Loads and Co-Location
values.quote: A failed stability screen > detailed EMT analysis > 6-9 months
values.note: EMT study duration for large loads (Brattle); FERC Order 2023 sets a 150-day cluster study for generators.

values.label: Large-load study, ERCOT
values.source_title: FERC Rulemakings on Large Loads and Co-Location
values.quote: ERCOT Batch Zero is a cluster process and timeline is 9 months for final study results
values.note: ERCOT Batch Zero study, 9 months; batches run about every 6 months.

values.label: Large-load study, MISO (ERAS)
values.source_title: MISO's first 10 power projects for expedited queue total 5.3 GW of new capacity
values.publisher: S&P Global Commodity Insights quoting MISO
values.quote: granted expedited generator interconnection agreements within 90 days
values.note: MISO ERAS 90-day target to an interconnection agreement / 30.44.

values.label: Large-load study, SPP (HILL)
values.source_title: SPP Status Update to Missouri PSC (Q3 2026)
values.quote: Time to study is 90 days for HILL, HILLGA, CHILL, and PAL
values.note: SPP HILL 90-day study / 30.44.

values.label: Utility energization wait, request to power
values.source_title: How long it actually takes to power a data center in 2026
values.publisher: Construction Owners Club citing JLL 2026 Global Data Center Outlook
values.quote: puts the national average wait at four years
values.note: National average wait for data-center power, 4 years (JLL 2026), in months; LBNL's generator median is 5 years request-to-COD.

values.label: Utility energization wait, Virginia (Dominion)
values.source_title: Data Centers Face Seven-Year Wait for Power Hookups in Virginia
values.publisher: Data Center Knowledge (citing Dominion Energy letter)
values.quote: 4 to 7 years for large data centers (over 100 MW)
values.note: Dominion letter: 4 to 7 years for new large loads, in months; 54 GW contracted against a 4.8 GW billing peak.

values.label: Large power transformer lead time
values.source_title: Making the connection: Meeting the electric T&D supply chain challenge (executive summary)
values.publisher: Wood Mackenzie with American Clean Power
values.quote: falling by 10 weeks to an average of 128 weeks
values.note: 128 weeks average, 80 to 210, in months; GSU transformers run 143 weeks.

values.label: Substation, need to in-service
values.source_title: PJM TEAC Dominion supplemental projects, Dec 8 2025 (Need/Solution meeting slides)
values.quote: Expected in-service date is 12/01/2027
values.note: a Dominion example in PJM filings, used as the US default

values.label: Transmission and line works
values.note: Utility line works are counted inside the energization wait above rather than as a separate task; a dedicated 345 kV line would add years (Grid Strategies: 6 to 10 years for large builds).

values.label: Gas turbine lead time
values.source_title: Siemens gas turbine backlog nears 70 GW as company expands manufacturing
values.publisher: Utility Dive quoting Siemens Energy earnings call
values.quote: lead times across the company now run three years or more
values.note: Siemens Energy: 3 or more years for new turbines, EIA's pre-shortage assumption was 2 years; Siemens is booked out to FY2028.

values.label: Reciprocating engine lead time
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Costs Jump 21% Since 2024 (reporting Cushman & Wakefield 2026 Data Center Development Cost Guide)
values.quote: Generators: 60 to 100 weeks
values.note: Generator sets are reciprocating engines: 60 to 100 weeks (Cushman & Wakefield) x 12/52.18.

values.label: Fuel cell lead time
values.source_title: Oracle, Bloom Energy Have Deal to Power Data Centers
values.publisher: POWER Magazine quoting Bloom Energy press release
values.quote: deliver on-site power for an entire data center within 90 days
values.note: Bloom Energy: 90 days, a vendor claim; / 30.44.

values.label: Solar and battery equipment lead time
values.source_title: Built But Not Ready: Construction Claims in the Data Center Boom
values.quote: Average U.S. equipment lead time is 42 weeks, 83% above 2019 levels
values.note: No solar or battery specific lead time found; the JLL US average equipment lead time of 42 weeks is used.

values.label: Onsite plant install, gas turbine
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: power infrastructure (Months 4–10)
values.note: Power infrastructure stage duration from an industry build guide (secondary), used for the onsite plant install.

values.label: Onsite plant install, recip
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: power infrastructure (Months 4–10)
values.note: Power infrastructure stage duration from an industry build guide (secondary), used for the onsite plant install.

values.label: Onsite plant install, fuel cell
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: power infrastructure (Months 4–10)
values.note: Power infrastructure stage duration from an industry build guide (secondary), used for the onsite plant install.

values.label: Onsite plant install, solar bess
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: power infrastructure (Months 4–10)
values.note: Power infrastructure stage duration from an industry build guide (secondary), used for the onsite plant install.

values.label: Grading, fence and road
values.note: No public duration found for the civil package alone; 3 months (2 to 4) is our assumption, inside the industry guide's construction phase.

values.label: Foundations
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: Foundation and Shell: Months 1–6
values.note: One third of the 6-month foundation-and-shell stage (industry guide, secondary).

values.label: Steel, roof and walls
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: Foundation and Shell: Months 1–6
values.note: Two thirds of the 6-month foundation-and-shell stage. JLARC puts a whole building at 12 to 18 months.

values.label: Electrical fit-out
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: power infrastructure (Months 4–10)
values.note: Power infrastructure stage (industry guide, secondary).

values.label: Mechanical fit-out
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: cooling systems (Months 6–12)
values.note: Cooling systems stage (industry guide, secondary).

values.label: Mechanical time factor, air cooling
values.note: No evidence that air-cooled fit-out is faster or slower; factor 1.

values.label: White space fit-out
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Timeline
values.quote: IT infrastructure (Months 10–18)
values.note: IT and white space stage (industry guide, secondary).

values.label: GPU rack install per 100 MW
values.source_title: Colossus (supercomputer)
values.quote: was constructed in 122 days
values.note: xAI Colossus: 122 days from start to the first training run for about 100,000 GPUs in an existing shell; / 30.44 and treated as the rack install and bring-up of roughly 100 MW. A benchmark, not a standard.

values.label: Cluster bring-up and burn-in
values.note: No public figure; one month is our assumption for burn-in after the racks are powered.

values.label: First phase share of racks
values.source_title: Applied Digital Completes Phase II Ready for Service at Polaris Forge 1
values.quote: Building 1 now operates at its full 100 MW critical IT load
values.note: Applied Digital brought a 100 MW building to ready-for-service in two 50 MW steps: 0.5.

values.label: Commissioning L1 to L2
values.source_title: Data Center Commissioning Levels
values.quote: 10–14 weeks across L1–L5
values.note: 30% of the 10 to 14 week L1 to L5 window (secondary).

values.label: Commissioning L3 to L4
values.source_title: Data Center Commissioning Levels
values.quote: 10–14 weeks across L1–L5
values.note: 70% of the 10 to 14 week L1 to L5 window (secondary).

values.label: Commissioning L5, integrated systems test
values.source_title: Global AI Data Center Construction 2026
values.quote: 10 to 14 weeks for a liquid-cooled AI hall
values.note: IST for a liquid-cooled AI hall, 10 to 14 weeks (secondary); air-cooled halls run 4 to 6 weeks.

values.label: Commissioning L5, integrated systems test, air-cooled
values.source_title: Global AI Data Center Construction 2026
values.quote: 4 to 6 weeks for a standard air-cooled hall
values.note: IST for an air-cooled hall, 4 to 6 weeks (secondary) x 12/52.18.

values.label: Tier IV certification visit after L5
values.source_title: Tier Certification Preparation
values.quote: a little more than a month after critical systems construction ends
values.note: Uptime Tier Certification of Constructed Facility: site visit after commissioning.

values.label: Electrical fit-out time factor, 2N
values.note: A second full power path adds equipment and testing; 10% more fit-out time is our assumption.

values.label: Duration scaling with load
values.note: Construction durations scale as (MW/100)^0.25, so 1 GW takes about 1.8x as long as 100 MW per task with the work phased across buildings. Our assumption, calibrated against the JLARC 12 to 18 month building and the 5-year Meta Hyperion campus.

values.label: MV switchgear lead time
values.source_title: Data Center Construction Costs Jump 21% Since 2024 (reporting Cushman & Wakefield 2026 Data Center Development Cost Guide)
values.quote: Medium-voltage switchgear: 38 to 63 weeks
values.note: 38 to 63 weeks (Cushman & Wakefield) x 12/52.18; Wood Mackenzie reports 44 weeks.

values.quote: Average U.S. equipment lead time is 42 weeks, 83% above 2019 levels

values.publisher: Wood Mackenzie with American Clean Power
values.quote: falling by 10 weeks to an average of 128 weeks

values.source_title: ERCOT Large Load Update, Senate Committee on Business & Commerce hearing
values.quote: Every ~6 months, all submitted requests are clustered and studied together
values.note: Missing one ERCOT large-load batch costs a full cadence, about 6 months.

values.label: Permit challenge

values.quote: Judge's ruling date: August 7, 2025 ... rezoning: December 2023

values.quote: about 10 months to the programme in Ireland and about 6 months in Virginia
values.note: Added grid energization time reported for Virginia (secondary).

values.label: GPU allocation delay
values.note: No public allocation statistic; one quarter is our assumption.
